tools.name: Add an object
tools.where: Add menu in the viewport header > Mesh
tools.what: Adds shapes such as a cube, sphere, plane or cylinder to the scene.

tools.name: Delete an object
tools.what: Removes the selected object from the scene.

tools.name: Move (grab)
tools.where: Object menu > Transform > Move, or the Move tool in the left toolbar
tools.what: Moves the selected object or mesh part. Add X, Y or Z to move along one direction.

tools.name: Rotate
tools.where: Object menu > Transform > Rotate, or the Rotate tool in the left toolbar
tools.what: Turns the selected object or mesh part.

tools.name: Scale
tools.where: Object menu > Transform > Scale, or the Scale tool in the left toolbar
tools.what: Makes the selection bigger or smaller. Add X, Y or Z to stretch in one direction.

tools.name: Extrude
tools.what: Pulls a selected face, edge or point outward to create new shape.

tools.name: Inset faces
tools.what: Creates a smaller face inside a selected face. Useful for windows and panels.

tools.name: Bevel edges
tools.what: Rounds off or chamfers sharp edges.

tools.name: Loop cut
tools.what: Adds a ring of new edges around a mesh so you have more to edit.

tools.name: Knife
tools.what: Cuts new edges across faces wherever you draw.

tools.name: Merge points
tools.what: Joins selected points (vertices) into one.

tools.name: Cut a hole (Boolean)
tools.where: Properties editor > Modifiers tab (wrench icon) > Add Modifier > Generate > Boolean
tools.what: Subtracts one object's shape from another, for example cutting a window or door hole through a wall.

tools.name: Smooth an object (Subdivision Surface)
tools.where: Properties editor > Modifiers tab > Add Modifier > Generate > Subdivision Surface
tools.what: Smooths and rounds a blocky object by adding more detail.

tools.name: Duplicate
tools.what: Makes a copy of the selected object. Move the mouse and click to place it.

tools.name: Join objects
tools.what: Combines several selected objects into one.

tools.name: Add colour (material)
tools.what: Gives the selected object a colour or surface look.

tools.name: See colours in the viewport
tools.where: Shading buttons at the top-right of the viewport (third sphere)
tools.what: Switches the viewport so colours and lighting are shown.

tools.name: Zoom to selected
tools.what: Zooms the view so the selected object fills the screen.

tools.name: Show everything
tools.what: Zooms out so every object in the scene is visible.

tools.name: Undo
tools.what: Reverses your last action.

tools.name: Select all / none
tools.what: Selects everything, or clears the selection.

tools.name: Switch Edit / Object mode
tools.where: Mode dropdown at the top-left of the viewport
tools.what: Switches between moving whole objects and editing their shape.

tools.name: Look through the camera
tools.what: Shows the scene the way the camera sees it.

tools.name: Render an image
tools.what: Creates a finished picture of your scene.

tools.name: Save your work
tools.what: Saves the Blender file so you do not lose your work.

tools.name: Search for any command
tools.what: Type a command's name and Blender finds it in the menus. The fastest way to find something you have forgotten.

tools.name: Repeat last action
tools.what: Does the last thing you did again, such as another extrude or another move.

tools.name: Adjust the last action
tools.where: Small panel at the bottom-left of the viewport after you do something
tools.what: Opens the settings of what you just did so you can change numbers like size, count or segments.

tools.name: Box select
tools.where: Select Box tool at the top of the left toolbar
tools.what: Selects everything inside a rectangle you drag.

tools.name: Vertex, edge or face select
tools.where: Three small buttons at the top-left of the viewport in Edit Mode
tools.what: Chooses whether you pick points, lines or flat faces.

tools.name: Select connected parts
tools.what: Selects a whole connected piece of the mesh in one go.

tools.name: Invert selection
tools.what: Selects everything that was not selected, and deselects what was.

tools.name: Fill a face
tools.where: Select points or edges, then Face menu > Make Edge/Face
tools.what: Creates a flat face between the selected points. Use it to close a hole.

tools.name: Delete mesh parts
tools.what: Deletes selected points, edges or faces. Pick what to delete from the little menu.

tools.name: Dissolve (delete without a hole)
tools.what: Removes points or edges but keeps the surface closed. Good for cleaning up.

tools.name: Separate into its own object
tools.what: Splits the selected part of a mesh off as a new object.

tools.name: Subdivide (add more cuts)
tools.where: Right click in Edit Mode > Subdivide
tools.what: Splits selected edges or faces into smaller pieces so you have more points to shape.

tools.name: Slide an edge
tools.what: Slides an edge loop along the surface without leaving the shape.

tools.name: Bridge two edge loops
tools.what: Joins two openings or loops with new faces, like a tunnel between them.

tools.name: Soft move (proportional editing)
tools.where: Circle icon in the viewport header
tools.what: Moves nearby points along with a smooth falloff, so shapes bend instead of poking out. Scroll the wheel while moving to change the range.

tools.name: Fix inside-out faces (normals)
tools.what: Turns faces the right way round so they stop looking dark or black.

tools.name: UV unwrap
tools.where: Select everything, then UV menu > Unwrap
tools.what: Flattens the surface so an image texture can be placed on it.

tools.name: Shade smooth
tools.what: Makes the surface look smooth instead of faceted without changing the shape.

tools.name: Apply scale and rotation
tools.where: Object menu > Apply > Scale (or All Transforms)
tools.what: Makes the current size and rotation the new normal. Fixes modifiers and bevels that look stretched.

tools.name: Set the origin point
tools.what: Moves the dot an object rotates and scales around. Choose Origin to Geometry to centre it.

tools.name: Parent objects (make a group that moves together)
tools.where: Select the child, then the parent last, then Object menu > Parent > Object
tools.what: Links objects so moving the parent moves the children too.

tools.name: Linked duplicate
tools.what: Makes a copy that shares its shape with the original, so editing one updates all.

tools.name: Hide and show objects
tools.shortcut: H hides, Alt + H shows all
tools.what: Hides the selected objects to clear the view, or brings every hidden object back.

tools.name: Rename an object
tools.where: Double click its name in the Outliner
tools.what: Gives the active object a clear name.

tools.name: Move to a collection (folder)
tools.where: Object menu > Collection > Move to Collection
tools.what: Sorts objects into groups in the Outliner so a big scene stays tidy.

tools.name: Isolate with Local View
tools.where: View menu > Local View > Toggle Local View
tools.what: Shows only the selected objects so you can work without distractions. Press again to come back.

tools.name: Orthographic or perspective
tools.what: Switches between a realistic view and a flat technical view with no depth distortion.

tools.name: Front, side and top views
tools.what: Jumps to straight-on views. Ctrl plus the key shows the opposite side. No numpad: use the View menu.

tools.name: Snapping
tools.where: Magnet icon in the viewport header
tools.what: Makes moved things click onto the grid, points or edges so everything lines up.

tools.name: 3D cursor
tools.where: Shift + Right click in the viewport, or View menu > Snap Cursor
tools.what: The red-and-white target where new objects appear. Shift + C puts it back at the centre.

tools.name: Pivot point
tools.where: Pivot dropdown in the viewport header
tools.what: Chooses what rotates and scales happen around: the object, the 3D cursor or the middle of a selection.

tools.name: Type exact numbers
tools.where: While moving, rotating or scaling, just type; or use the Item tab in the sidebar
tools.what: Type a number right after G, R or S to be precise. Example: S, 2, Enter doubles the size.

tools.name: Show or hide the side panels
tools.what: N opens the sidebar with exact position, rotation and size. T shows the toolbar.

tools.name: Wireframe and X-ray
tools.where: Shading buttons at the top-right of the viewport
tools.what: See through objects to select hidden points, or view only the edges.

tools.name: Mirror (symmetry)
tools.where: Properties editor > wrench tab > Add Modifier > Generate > Mirror
tools.what: Builds the other half of a shape automatically, so you only model one side.

tools.name: Array (repeat copies)
tools.where: Properties editor > wrench tab > Add Modifier > Generate > Array
tools.what: Repeats an object in a row or a staircase with a few settings. Great for fences, stairs and windows.

tools.name: Solidify (give thickness)
tools.where: Properties editor > wrench tab > Add Modifier > Generate > Solidify
tools.what: Turns a flat surface into something with real thickness, like a wall or a sheet.

tools.name: Bevel modifier (round all edges)
tools.where: Properties editor > wrench tab > Add Modifier > Generate > Bevel
tools.what: Rounds every edge at once, so objects catch light like real ones.

tools.name: Apply a modifier
tools.where: Arrow next to the modifier name in the wrench tab > Apply
tools.what: Bakes the modifier into the actual mesh so you can edit the result.

tools.name: Add a light
tools.what: Adds a Point, Sun, Spot or Area light so your scene is lit when rendered.

tools.name: Add a camera
tools.where: Add menu > Camera. Ctrl + Alt + Numpad 0 snaps it to your current view
tools.what: Adds the camera that decides what the final picture shows.

tools.name: Insert a keyframe (animate)
tools.where: Hover the viewport, press I; or right click a value > Insert Keyframe
tools.what: Records the position, rotation or size at the current frame so it can animate over time.

tools.name: Play or pause animation
tools.where: Play button in the Timeline at the bottom
tools.what: Plays the animation from the current frame. Press again to stop.

tools.name: Open a file
tools.what: Opens a saved .blend file. Open Recent is the quickest way back to your last project.

tools.name: Save as a new file
tools.what: Saves a copy under a new name, which is handy for versions and backups.
